meta.title: Who really said "There are only two ways of telling the complete truth — anonymously and posthumously"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes, Thomas Sowell. Quote Investigator traced this quip to his July 1985 syndicated newspaper column. A 1996 credit to teacher Susan Ohanian came later.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'There are only two ways of telling the complete truth — anonymously and posthumously'?
meta.ogDescription: Thomas Sowell wrote it in a July 1985 newspaper column, per Quote Investigator. A 1996 book later credited a reworded version to Susan Ohanian.

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: Born 1930 · American economist, Hoover Institution senior fellow
answer.sourceLine: It appears word for word in Sowell’s Scripps-Howard newspaper column, printed in The Stuart News (Stuart, Florida) on 5 July 1985. The line sits in a list of “There are only two…” quips. Quote Investigator ↗ located the column and credits Sowell.

source.heading: Where it comes from

docMeta.dd: “Life is just a two-way street” (newspaper column, Scripps-Howard News Service)
The Stuart News, Stuart, Florida — 5 July 1985, page A5

source.excerpt:
There are only two kinds of schools — those that keep up with the latest educational trends and those that teach.

There are only two ways of telling the complete truth — anonymously and posthumously.

There are only two kinds of gamblers — those who say they have lost more than they have won and those who lie about it.
trail: 1985: Sowell’s syndicated column, printed in The Stuart News on 5 July, includes the line word for word (Quote Investigator ↗).
1986: Robert Byrne’s collection The Third and Possibly the Best 637 Best Things Anybody Ever Said prints it credited to Thomas Sowell (QI ↗; the book at the Internet Archive ↗).
1996: Rosalie Maggio’s The New Beacon Book of Quotations by Women credits Susan Ohanian’s Ask Ms. Class with a reworded version: “two ways to tell the one hundred percent truth” (QI ↗).
2000: Random House Webster’s Wit & Humor Quotationary gives the original wording under Thomas Sowell (QI ↗).
source.cutTag: Three consecutive items from the column
source.excerptNote: These are the three consecutive items Quote Investigator transcribes from Sowell’s July 1985 column. The column was a long list of quips and adages.

author.name: Thomas Sowell
author.heading: About Thomas Sowell
author.bio: Thomas Sowell was born in Gastonia, North Carolina, in 1930. He is an economist, economic historian and social theorist, and a senior fellow at Stanford’s Hoover Institution since 1980. For decades his syndicated newspaper column was known for pithy one-liners, until he ended it in December 2016. That reputation is why so many clever lines, real and invented, get pinned on him.

misattribution.heading: The other names on it
misattribution.intro: The line is genuinely Sowell’s. Some quotation books and posts credit someone else, usually because of a later reworded version.

items.why: Rosalie Maggio’s The New Beacon Book of Quotations by Women (1996) credits the U.S. teacher and writer’s Ask Ms. Class with “There are only two ways to tell the one hundred percent truth: anonymously and posthumously.” Quote Investigator ↗ concludes that Sowell’s 1985 statement keeps priority.

items.who: Mrs. Waagen (Red Cross, quoted in Calgary)
items.why: In 1923 The Morning Albertan quoted her as saying any book about her Red Cross experiences would “either be published anonymously or posthumously.” QI cites this as a related remark, not Sowell’s “two ways of telling the complete truth” formula (QI ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: Thomas Sowell published the line in his syndicated column, printed in The Stuart News on 5 July 1985 (Quote Investigator ↗).

context.heading: Why it matters
lead: Sowell is one of the internet’s favorite names to hang a clever line on, so the default assumption should be fabrication. This one turns out to be real. The line was one entry in a column made up of quips and adages, and it sat between jokes about schools that “teach” and gamblers who “lie about it.” Quotation collectors picked it up within a year.

Sowell has had to disown fake material himself. In a 2008 column he wrote that “a whole column has been made up and circulated in a chain letter on the Internet” under his name, and that anyone can check his real columns (“An Internet Fraud,” Creators ↗).
detailsBody: The 1996 version credited to Susan Ohanian says “the one hundred percent truth” where Sowell said “the complete truth,” and it uses a colon instead of a dash. Quote Investigator calls it “a very similar remark” and dates it after Sowell’s column (QI ↗).
